label: sim-dsa-bst-copier-2
assignment: Binary Search Tree for Exam Roll Numbers
source: simulated demo student (persona: copier) run through the real platform

testResults.name: Sorted input makes a tall tree

viva.summary: The student has implemented a functional BST but lacks a conceptual understanding of tree traversal properties and height calculation. They struggled to trace the logic of their own methods during the viva.

rubric.revise_next: Review how tree height is defined and practice tracing the path to the minimum and maximum nodes in a BST.

questions.answer: Sir wo, shayad tree ki depth count karne ke liye hai, minus one is liye kyunke shayad index zero se start hota hai ya koi logic hai, mujhe sahi se nahi pata.
questions.feedback: You identified that it relates to counting depth, but you need to understand that -1 is used so that a single-node tree results in a height of 0.
questions.prompt: In your `height` method, what is the purpose of the base case `return -1 if not node else ...` and why is -1 the correct value for an empty tree?

questions.answer: pata nahi sir, shayad 3 ya 4 return karta hai.
questions.feedback: Your prediction was incorrect; you should trace the tree structure to see that a root with two children has a height of 1.
questions.prompt: What will your code return if you call build([10, 5, 15]).height()?

questions.answer: Sir, I think bas root se left side pe jate hain shayad, ya phir shayad root ko traverse karte hain, pata nahi sir.
questions.feedback: To find the maximum value, you should traverse to the rightmost node instead of the left.
questions.prompt: If you wanted to add a 'max()' method to return the largest roll number in the tree, what logic would you use to find it? Explain the traversal path you would take starting from the root.
